unit: One fixed workload of the selected suite: either a Spectrum workload record with its generator seed, or the checkpoint-micro trace for one suite seed. Development has two Spectrum and two checkpoint-micro workloads; the disjoint final suite has three of each. Every workload reports the same metric set. Each Spectrum workload has five one-second observations and each checkpoint-micro workload five 400-round traces per compared variant.

metrics.name: correctness
metrics.means: Successful oracle, lifetime, reclamation and multi-height rollback checks (checkpoint-micro) and every restore check during real execution (Spectrum: height, code position, top() and every item), with finite positive output.
metrics.source: checkpoint_bench.cpp for checkpoint-micro workloads; the Spectrum harness in lib/transaction/evm-transaction.cpp for Spectrum workloads.
metrics.clears_when: Candidate passes all patch, compile, oracle, lifetime, allocation, and execution gates; the reference must also pass. No correctness tolerance.

metrics.name: committed_tps
metrics.means: Workload throughput: committed transactions per second on a Spectrum workload; completed rounds per second (1e9 / end-to-end nanoseconds per round, covering every save with its writes and every restore with its access mix) on a checkpoint-micro workload.
metrics.source: The authentic Spectrum bench commit statistic (five rotated runs) or the checkpoint_bench.cpp end-to-end timer (five traces).
metrics.clears_when: min(candidate five throughput observations) > max(reference five throughput observations). All observations must be finite and positive.
metrics.tolerance: No fixed percentage band is inferred from aggregate historical scores. Require strict separation of the five observed timing ranges; equality, overlap, or fewer than five observations fails.

metrics.name: checkpoint_create_ns
metrics.means: Nanoseconds per created checkpoint: save_checkpoint() plus storing the checkpoint, averaged over every creation in a Spectrum run, or over the 400-round trace on a checkpoint-micro workload.
metrics.source: The Spectrum harness timer around save_checkpoint() during real execution, or checkpoint_bench.cpp.
metrics.clears_when: max(candidate five create-ns observations) < min(reference five create-ns observations). All observations must be finite and positive.
metrics.tolerance: Strict observed-range separation across five complete 400-round traces; equality or overlap fails. No fabricated hardware-independent nanosecond/percentage tolerance.

metrics.name: checkpoint_restore_ns
metrics.means: Nanoseconds per restored checkpoint: load_checkpoint() alone, averaged over every rollback in a Spectrum run, or over the 400-round trace on a checkpoint-micro workload.
metrics.source: The Spectrum harness timer around load_checkpoint() during real execution, or checkpoint_bench.cpp.
metrics.clears_when: max(candidate five restore-ns observations) < min(reference five restore-ns observations). All observations must be finite and positive.
metrics.tolerance: Strict observed-range separation across five complete 400-round traces; equality or overlap fails.

metrics.name: retained_bytes_per_checkpoint
metrics.means: Bytes retained per live checkpoint: on a checkpoint-micro workload the peak tracked requested bytes over 16 simultaneous checkpoints; on a Spectrum workload the net heap bytes the executing thread holds since its transaction's execution state was created (harness records excluded), divided by the live checkpoints, averaged over checkpoint creations.
metrics.source: The allocation tracker in checkpoint_bench.cpp, or jemalloc per-thread allocated/deallocated counters read by the Spectrum harness.
metrics.clears_when: max(candidate five retained-byte observations) < min(reference five retained-byte observations). The exact integer capacity metric must decrease; equality fails.
metrics.tolerance: No tolerance; strict separation of the five observations. The checkpoint-micro value is an exact requested-byte count; the Spectrum value depends on the executed transaction mix and is not exact.

beats_reference: 1 iff every declared metric passes for every workload in the fixed selected suite; otherwise 0. The continuous score and its cached upstream anchor remain separate and cannot turn a failed metric into a pass.

solver_feedback.name: committed_tps
solver_feedback.means: Geometric mean over development workload medians of the candidate committed TPS.
solver_feedback.reveals_reference: no — an absolute candidate-only scalar, with no workload identities or comparison-derived values

solver_feedback.name: checkpoint_create_ns
solver_feedback.means: Median of the first candidate creation-time profile per development seed, in nanoseconds.
solver_feedback.reveals_reference: no — an absolute candidate-only scalar, with no workload identities or comparison-derived values

solver_feedback.name: checkpoint_restore_ns
solver_feedback.means: Median of the first candidate restoration-time profile per development seed, in nanoseconds.
solver_feedback.reveals_reference: no — an absolute candidate-only scalar, with no workload identities or comparison-derived values

solver_feedback.name: retained_bytes_per_checkpoint
solver_feedback.means: Maximum of the first candidate retained-byte profiles over development seeds.
solver_feedback.reveals_reference: no — an absolute candidate-only scalar, with no workload identities or comparison-derived values

withheld: All reference measurements and reference scores.
Per-workload identities, individual pass/fail decisions, timing samples, margins, speedups, and ratios to any private reference.
All hidden-final measurements; development feedback contains only the selected development suite.
statement_sentences: The beat-reference flag is separate from the continuous score. Every workload, each Spectrum workload and each checkpoint-micro workload (one per suite seed: four development workloads or six final workloads), reports the same metric set and must pass correctness and independently improve throughput (committed TPS on a Spectrum workload; completed rounds per second of the timed loop on a checkpoint-micro workload), checkpoint creation time, checkpoint restoration time, and retained bytes per checkpoint. No workload is exempt from any metric. For every performance metric, all five candidate measurements must strictly outperform all five same-workload reference measurements: the minimum candidate throughput must exceed the maximum reference throughput, and the maximum candidate creation time, restoration time, and retained bytes must each be below the corresponding minimum reference value. Equality or overlapping timing ranges do not pass. An invalid evaluation makes every comparison fail; no workload is removed. Development feedback exposes candidate-only aggregate measurements and per-metric workload pass/fail counts and percentages, never the individual decisions or reference measurements.
comments: Repair of the exported task missing Stage-2 beat-spec contract. Existing aggregate equality-as-win was invalid. The upstream patch, generated workloads, original first-profile measurements and continuous score formula are unchanged. Four extra checkpoint traces per seed and compared variant are necessary because the original one observation per seed provides no per-workload noise estimate; no extra Spectrum run or build is added. Subsequent profile order rotates by seed/repetition. Existing hardware, per-process limits and total evaluation budget remain authoritative. Strict separation is a conservative empirical gate, not a claim of a calibrated confidence level or that five observations bound all future timing noise. Current/reference self-comparison need not beat itself. Uniform metric set (Preview #646, 2026-10-25): every Spectrum workload and every checkpoint-micro workload reports throughput, create, restore, retained bytes and correctness, and the gate and composite apply to all of them; the definitions of create and restore time are unchanged (save_checkpoint() plus storing it; load_checkpoint() alone). Spectrum checkpoint metrics are measured by the harness around the backend during real execution; the micro trace adds an end-to-end timer over saves with their writes and restores with an interpreter-like access mix, plus multi-height top()/pop()/get() rollback checks. Earlier runs are not comparable across this change.
